title: Sunshine Pictures IPO sees strong retail demand on Day 1 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The initial public offering of Sunshine Pictures Ltd. closed its first day on Tuesday with an overall subscription of 4.33 times, driven primarily by retail and non-institutional investors, while qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) remained largely on the sidelines.

As of close on August 18, the IPO received bids for 2,37,74,711 shares against 54,86,051 shares on offer. The retail individual investor (RII) category was subscribed 5.98 times, with bids for 1,64,07,216 shares against 27,43,023 on offer. The non-institutional investor (NII) segment saw the strongest response, subscribing 6.23 times overall, with the sub-₹10 lakh category clocking 9.34 times subscription.

In contrast, the QIB category registered a near-absent response, subscribed just 0.03 times with bids for only 45,346 shares against 15,67,436 on offer. Foreign institutional investors and domestic financial institutions together accounted for 5,576 bids, with mutual funds recording zero participation on day one.

The IPO, which opened on August 18 and closes on August 20, offers shares in the price band of ₹342–360, with a post-issue market capitalisation of ₹1,121 crore at the upper end. The total issue size is ₹282 crore, comprising a fresh issue of ₹173 crore and an offer for sale of ₹109 crore. Net proceeds from the fresh issue are earmarked for working capital requirements.

SBI Securities, in its IPO note, has recommended investors avoid the issue. Analysts noted that the company has recorded negative revenue, EBITDA, and PAT CAGR of 25.4 per cent, 8.6 per cent, and 13.4 per cent respectively over FY24–FY26. At the upper price band, the issue is valued at a P/E multiple of 27.8x on post-issue FY26 earnings, which analysts flagged as expensive given the high dependence on box office performance and inherent unpredictability of content success.
